person.name: Grant Lindburg
person.tagline: Systems engineer with a designer's hands. Twelve years across backend, agency interaction design, WebGL, and now agentic AI.

meta.title: Grant Lindburg — Engineer, Chicago
meta.description: Grant Lindburg builds AI systems, 3D web experiences, and the architecture underneath them. Twelve years of work, shown era by era.

eras.title: AI Systems
eras.summary: Agentic pipelines, tool-using assistants, and an engineering practice where the model is a collaborator in planning, building, and review.

projects.title: Agentic research pipeline
projects.outcome: Planner/executor agents with tool use and an eval harness. Sample entry: swap in a real project.

projects.title: Generative shader studies
projects.outcome: Real-time GPU experiments with live parameter overlays, published as short studies.

projects.title: AI-assisted engineering practice
projects.outcome: This site: brainstormed, specced, and shipped test-first with an AI collaborator. Source is public.

eras.lesson: The architecture is the prompt. Boundaries, contracts, and evals matter more than the model.

eras.title: Published Studios & Bill Niacin
eras.summary: Leading a small team of self-taught developers building sites for artists, brands, and Chicago businesses. Under the Bill Niacin name: 3D, WebGL, and interactive work where the code is part of the art.

projects.title: Bill's Happy Place
projects.outcome: A living-garden portfolio: zoom from an aerial garden out to a globe with client sites orbiting as portals.

projects.title: We Real Cool (For School)
projects.outcome: Apparel storefront for a Chicago label.

projects.title: Sydney Jackson
projects.outcome: Artist portfolio with an editorial, photo-first layout.

projects.title: DRAMA
projects.outcome: Minimal apparel shop with product-forward grid.

projects.title: ember.
projects.outcome: Booking site for a sauna on the Chicago Riverwalk.

eras.lesson: Delight is a performance budget. Every effect has to earn its frame.

eras.title: Leo Burnett
eras.summary: Three years inside a global agency: prototypes, motion, and production front-ends for household brands, where the craft is making the polished thing feel effortless.

projects.title: Campaign front-ends
projects.outcome: Prototype-to-production sites and microsites for brand campaigns.

projects.title: Interactive prototypes
projects.outcome: Clickable concepts for pitches and testing: the fastest path from an idea to something in hand.

projects.title: Motion & micro-interaction
projects.outcome: Transitions and feedback that explain state instead of decorating it.

eras.lesson: Restraint reads as confidence. Motion should explain, not decorate.
